subject: chemistry
title: Inside the Atom
welcome_lead: Tiny but mighty: the atom holds three even tinier particles with very different jobs.
meta_desc: Explore protons, neutrons and electrons in this KS3 chemistry adventure on the atom.
final_note: You now know the three sub-atomic particles and where they live.

concepts.def: The smallest particle of an element.
Neutral (no charge) particle in the nucleus.
Dense centre of an atom holding protons and neutrons.
Energy levels where electrons are found.

walkthroughs.body_html:
An atom contains:

Protons (+) in the nucleus.
Neutrons (0) in the nucleus.
Electrons (−) orbiting the nucleus in shells.

The nucleus is tiny but holds nearly all the mass. Electrons fly around it in shells, with lots of empty space in between.

Atoms are mostly empty!

In a neutral atom, the number of protons equals the number of electrons, so positive and negative balance to zero.

The number of protons defines which element it is — this is the atomic number.

options: Proton
Neutron
Electron
Nucleus

mcqs.q: Where is the mass of an atom mainly found?
options: In the electron shells
In the nucleus
In the empty space
Spread evenly

mcqs.q: What is the relationship between two enantiomers?
options: They are non-superimposable mirror images that rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions but have identical chemical and physical properties otherwise.
Enantiomers are the same molecule drawn differently on paper.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
Enantiomers have different boiling points and react completely differently with all reagents.

mcqs.q: Why is the hydration enthalpy of a small, highly charged ion very exothermic?
options: Small/highly charged ions form strong ion-dipole attractions with water molecules, releasing a large amount of energy.
Enantiomers are the same molecule drawn differently on paper.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
Hydration enthalpy only depends on the size of the ion, not its charge.

mcqs.q: How do alkenes typically react with bromine?
options: Bromine substitutes for a hydrogen on the alkene, releasing HBr.
The alkene polymerises with bromine to form a long chain.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
By electrophilic addition — bromine adds across the double bond to form a dibromoalkane.
